scope: every sense authored in tick 6 (shard 15), drawn complete rather than sampled
authoring: parallel family-author agents, Opus 5 at xhigh, rubric verbatim, prompts identical across all 23 families
comparability: fully comparable to censuses 007 and 008 on both instruments
pre_read_checks: tone_lint clean including the new family-inconsistent rule; family_apply axis-direction check clean after three reversals

entries.definition: having a strong desire for success or achievement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain name for the desire itself, favourable but only mildly, and carrying no fault until *overambitious* attaches one.

entries.definition: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and cool — it registers the reaching for recognition or advancement without any verdict on it, where *aspiring* sounds warm.

entries.definition: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Treats the reaching as a credit to the person, though it promises nothing beyond the wanting and the effort themselves.

entries.definition: strongly motivated to succeed
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the motivation as something that has hold of the person, so it lands closer to a diagnosis than to the compliment *determined* pays.

entries.definition: strongly motivated to succeed
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The approving way to say it — the motivation reads as steadiness of will rather than as pressure, which is what separates it from *driven*.

entries.definition: strongly motivated to succeed
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Keeps the admiration but not the comfort: the motivation is felt as something pushing from behind rather than chosen.

entries.definition: unfulfilled or frustrated in realizing an ambition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, and it files the ambition as one that came to nothing — the same verdict *would-be* delivers far more bluntly.

entries.definition: excessively ambitious
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the quantity of the ambition into the fault, condemning as excess exactly what *ambitious* merely reports.

entries.definition: marked by aggressive ambition and energy and initiative
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: States the aggression as a quality of the person and still counts the energy and initiative in, so it stings less than *pushy*.

entries.definition: marked by aggressive ambition and energy and initiative
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The complaint form of that same drive: the energy is conceded, the aggression is what the word is actually for.

entries.definition: desiring or striving for recognition or advancement
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts its weight on the wanting rather than on any force behind it, making it the gentlest way to say what *pushy* says harshly.

entries.definition: unfulfilled or frustrated in realizing an ambition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Deflating in one stroke: it grants the ambition and withholds the achievement in the same breath.

entries.definition: providing or experiencing physical well-being or relief (‘comfy’ is informal)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain baseline of the set, covering both the chair and the person sitting in it, without the warmth *cozy* adds.
examples: made himself comfortable in an armchair
the antihistamine made her feel more comfortable

entries.definition: providing or experiencing physical well-being or relief (‘comfy’ is informal)
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and fond where *comfortable* is plain, claiming no more ease than it does — only a softer way of saying it.
examples: made himself comfortable in an armchair
the antihistamine made her feel more comfortable

entries.definition: enjoying or affording comforting warmth and shelter especially in a small space
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Carries exactly *cozy*'s sheltered warmth; the difference is one of spelling, not of force.

entries.definition: enjoying or affording comforting warmth and shelter especially in a small space
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds warmth and shelter to *comfortable*'s bare ease, the comfort of being enclosed and kept warm.
examples: a cozy nook near the fire

entries.definition: affording comfort
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The thinnest word here: it says a thing affords comfort and stops, with none of *cozy*'s warmth or *soothing*'s relief.
examples: soft light that was easy on the eyes

entries.definition: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Locates the comfort in the feeling of home, so it praises a place for putting you at ease rather than for warmth alone as *cozy* does.

entries.definition: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same home-feeling approval as *homelike*, settled and unshowy — the praise is for the ease of the place, not its grandeur.

entries.definition: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal where *homelike* is plainly descriptive, saying the same home-comfort more casually.

entries.definition: having a feeling of home; cozy and comfortable
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A spelling variant of *homey*, identical in its fond, informal warmth toward a place that feels like home.

entries.definition: enjoying or affording comforting warmth and shelter especially in a small space
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the weight on close fit — comfort from being tucked into a small space rather than merely warmed, more bodily than *cozy*.

entries.definition: affording physical relief
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Comfort framed as active relief — where *easy* merely affords comfort, this one implies a physical discomfort being eased.
examples: a soothing ointment for her sunburn

entries.definition: discontented as toward authority
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Loyalty withdrawn: the discontent is pointed at authority but goes no further than turning away, where *rebellious* has already moved against it.

entries.definition: showing or experiencing dissatisfaction or restless longing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Covers the same ground as *discontented* - dissatisfaction or restless longing alike - but the clipped form makes it read as a fixed condition rather than a passing mood.
examples: saw many discontent faces in the room

entries.definition: showing or experiencing dissatisfaction or restless longing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain state-word of the family, reaching over both settled dissatisfaction and the restless longing for something else, and passing verdict on neither.

entries.definition: in a state of sulky dissatisfaction
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Belittling - the sulk in it makes the grievance look like a mood, so the complaint gets dismissed along with the complainer.

entries.definition: in a state of sulky dissatisfaction
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports the same sulky state with a straighter face, letting the mood be inferred where *disgruntled* puts it on display.

entries.definition: discontented as toward authority
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on the ill feeling itself rather than on the falling-away *disaffected* names, and stays stiffer and more formal in doing so.

entries.definition: discontented as toward authority
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faintly contemptuous - it makes standing against authority into a disposition the person carries, not a response they had.

entries.definition: discontented as toward authority
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hottest of the authority-facing senses, discontent that has broken into open defiance instead of sitting in itself like *disaffected*.

entries.definition: worried and uneasy
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Unease that will not sit still - the worry is felt as agitation rather than as a grievance against anything in particular.

entries.definition: worried and uneasy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most detached way of naming the worried unease, stating it as a condition and holding nothing against the person in it.

entries.definition: worried and uneasy
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and unemphatic beside *restless*, registering the same worry and unease without any of the movement.

entries.definition: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and graceless force: the indecency is out in the open with no refinement over it, where *indecent* only names the offence.

entries.definition: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest-sounding word for the same conspicuous, tasteless indecency, its plainness softening what *gross* spits out.

entries.definition: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Registers revulsion rather than disapproval, the indecency coarse enough to sicken, and the word is the flinch.

entries.definition: offensive to good taste especially in sexual matters
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's flat verdict of offence to good taste, sexual matters foremost though not only those, condemning without the flagrancy *crude* insists on.
examples: an earthy but not indecent story

entries.definition: verging on the indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest reproof here, indecency approached but not arrived at, so it rebukes where *obscene* accuses.

entries.definition: designed to incite to indecency or lust
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest charge in the family: not merely offensive but built to incite indecency or lust, design rather than effect.
examples: the dance often becomes flagrantly obscene

entries.definition: tending to suggest something improper or indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Works by implication, pointing toward the improper or the indecent without stating it, and accuses more lightly than *crude* for that reason.

entries.definition: conspicuously and tastelessly indecent
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Passes judgement on the sensibility behind the indecency as much as on the act, a verdict of cheapness that *earthy* declines to pass.
examples: full of language so vulgar it should have been edited

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Hears the quickness as responsiveness rather than pure pace, the coolest and least showy way of saying it.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Crisp and businesslike - the pace earns approval on its efficiency alone, with none of the buoyancy *merry* adds.
examples: a brisk walk in the park

entries.definition: lively and brisk
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Takes both halves at once, the animation of *lively* with the crispness of *brisk*, and stays mild where *rattling* is emphatic.

entries.definition: acting with vigor
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Vigor with push and direction behind it - force applied to something, not energy on display as in *lively*.
examples: responsibility turned the spoiled playboy into a driving young executive

entries.definition: possessing or exerting or displaying energy
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain term of the family, covering energy merely held as readily as energy spent or shown, and approving mildly without insisting.
examples: an energetic fund raiser for the college
it caused an energetic chemical reaction

entries.definition: providing a relatively large amount of energy upon undergoing a chemical reaction
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A measurement rather than a compliment, rating what a reaction yields and carrying none of the approval its neighbours do.

entries.definition: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and the most admiring of the three, treating the unflagging vitality as a quality of character rather than a rate of output.
examples: an indefatigable advocate of equal rights

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warmer than *brisk*, since the quickness comes with visible animation rather than a merely good rate.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Makes speed sound light and unforced where *brisk* makes it sound efficient.

entries.definition: characterized by energetic bodily activity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the energy in the body and stops there - a description of what the activity is, not a verdict on it as *lively* is.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: An intensifier more than a description, pushing quickness toward headlong in a way *brisk* never does.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Informal and clipped - quickness with an edge on it, sharper and less dignified than *brisk*.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Showier than *brisk*, admiring the sheer unchecked vigor of the pace rather than its neatness.

entries.definition: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Plainer than *indefatigable*, praising the sustained action itself without dressing it up.

entries.definition: showing sustained enthusiastic action with unflagging vitality
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises what does not happen - the enthusiasm never dips - so it commends steadiness where *tireless* commends capacity.

entries.definition: quick and energetic
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most informal of these, light and almost playful, carrying none of the weight *driving* does.

entries.definition: having unsymmetrical parts or unequal dimensions or measurements
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Technical and cool: it states that parts are out of symmetry or dimensions come out unequal, and stops there without calling either a defect.

entries.definition: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a contest or the contestants in it, this puts the fault in the pairing itself - these two should never have been set against each other.

entries.definition: not equal or interchangeable in value, quantity, or significance
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat denial rather than a complaint - the two are not equal and not interchangeable in value, quantity or significance, and the gap between them goes unjudged.

entries.definition: having a better than even chance of success
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one member where the imbalance is good news: the chance of success runs better than even, so the tilt reads as advantage rather than defect.

entries.definition: debits and credits are not equal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strictly the ledger sense - debits failing to answer credits - which lands as an error in the books rather than as a neutral difference.

entries.definition: poorly balanced or matched in quantity or value or measure
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries a fault inside the measurement - poorly balanced or matched, not merely different - where *nonequivalent* only records that the quantities fail to agree.

entries.definition: not caused to be equal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British spelling of *unequalized* and just as unjudging - it says only that nothing was made equal.

entries.definition: not caused to be equal
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Points at what was not done rather than at the result: no levelling has been applied, where *unequal* passes judgement on the gap that remains.

entries.definition: (of a contest or contestants) not fairly matched as opponents
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Softer than *mismatched* for the same unfair contest: it notes that the thing tilts one way without condemning the making of the match.
examples: vaudeville … waged an uneven battle against the church

entries.definition: having unsymmetrical parts or unequal dimensions or measurements
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain-spoken counterpart to *anisometric* for the same condition of parts or measurements, describing the lack of match rather than complaining of it.

entries.definition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and two-sided, covering both the meaning that was never spelled out and the one that sits in a thing's nature, where *unspoken* reaches only the first.
examples: an implicit agreement not to raise the subject
there was implicit criticism in his voice
anger was implicit in the argument
the oak is implicit in the acorn

entries.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A relational phrase rather than a quality — it must name the thing the sense is lodged in, which the bare adjectives beside it need not do.

entries.definition: implied though not directly expressed; inherent in the nature of something
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Built as a negation, it frames the same implicitness as a shortfall in the telling, where *implicit* frames it as a property of the thing.

entries.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The firmest claim of the three: not hidden by accident but built into what the thing is, and so not detachable from it.

entries.definition: implied by or inferred from actions or statements
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain everyday word for a meaning that rides along with an act or a statement without being spoken, lighter in weight than *tacit*.

entries.definition: implied by or inferred from actions or statements
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal, and it treats the unspoken meaning as settled and binding — something one is held to, which *silent* does not insist on.

entries.definition: in the nature of something though not readily apparent
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Puts the sense beneath a surface rather than inside a nature, implying something could be uncovered, where *inherent* makes it permanent.

entries.definition: implied by or inferred from actions or statements
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Adds successful uptake: the meaning was not merely implied but taken up on both sides, where *tacit* says only that it went unsaid.
examples: the understood provisos of a custody agreement

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and general — it says the thing found no outward form at all, without insisting that words in particular were what went missing.
examples: the unexpressed terms of the agreement

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plainest of the negatives, and it carries a faint sense of something held back, where *unexpressed* is a flat report.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The most loaded of the plain negatives — what is unspoken feels present and deliberately left alone, where *unstated* is only a blank.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Dry and procedural, marking the absence the way one notes a missing entry, beside the more human *unsaid*.
examples: his action is clear but his reason remains unstated

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Elevated and faintly literary, shaping the omission as something never let out rather than merely never recorded.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The British spelling of the same clinical term, identical in force to *unverbalized*.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical in register, framing the gap as a failure to convert into words rather than a silence with any weight to it.

entries.definition: not made explicit
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Implies a voice was available and went unused, which gives it more pull than the flat *unverbalized*.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild - the expression stumbles without collapsing, and no verdict is passed on the ability behind it, unlike *inept*.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Heavier than *awkward* - the expression is not merely ungainly but handled with a thick hand.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the expression for weight and unwieldiness, landing on the shape of the thing where *clumsy* lands on the handling.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blames the selection rather than the person, faulting the words picked where *inept* faults whoever picked them.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The dry, measured option - it records an expression as not fitting, with none of *clumsy*'s picture of bungled handling.

entries.definition: not elegant or graceful in expression
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The hardest of these words - it shifts the fault from the phrasing to the ability behind it, so gracelessness reads as incompetence.
examples: if the rumor is true, can anything be more inept than to repeat it now?

entries.definition: not appropriate in application; defective
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and softened - it marks a thing as both misapplied and defective while keeping an apologetic surface, where *inept* simply condemns.
examples: the infelicitous typesetting was due to illegible copy

entries.definition: unsuitable or regrettable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest wording available - it calls a thing unsuitable and regrettable at once, treating the fault as bad luck rather than bad work.

entries.definition: most unfortunate or miserable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Superlative and unsparing, pushing misfortune to its floor where *unfortunate* only notes that luck ran out.
examples: the most abject slaves joined in the revolt

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Delivers the verdict in one flat syllable, calling an event doomed where *calamitous* spells out the wreckage.
examples: the stock market crashed on Black Friday

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sizes the event by the wreckage it brings and says so at volume, where *black* passes the same sentence without raising its voice.

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word for ruin at full scale, doing the work of *calamitous* without its air of grandeur.
examples: the battle was a disastrous end to a disastrous campaign

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the condition as something stripped away, whether the security lost is literal shelter or inward footing, where *homeless* only reports the absence.
examples: made a living out of shepherding dispossessed people from one country to another

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the ruin as finished business, the consequences ending things rather than merely wrecking them as *disastrous* allows.
examples: such doctrines, if true, would be absolutely fatal to my theory
it is fatal to enter any war without the will to win it

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weights the ruin with inevitability, as though the outcome were settled before the event, a solemnity *disastrous* never claims.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Almost fond pity for someone luck keeps failing, entirely free of the contempt in *pathetic*.

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat naming term, covering the person without a roof and the one without spiritual anchorage alike, and carrying none of the grievance in *dispossessed*.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Wretchedness thick enough to be uncomfortable to look at, far heavier than the light sympathy of *hapless*.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest of these, granting that the pity is deserved and stopping there, where *pathetic* adds scorn to it.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pity curdled into contempt, looking down at what it pities in a way *piteous* never does.
examples: the shabby room struck her as extraordinarily pathetic

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elevated and unmixed, the suffering moving whoever sees it rather than lowering the sufferer as *pathetic* does.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sits on the hinge, able to ask for pity or to grant it while withholding respect, where *piteous* only asks.

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps a bleak physical picture even when the exposure it names is inward, which makes it starker than *homeless*.

entries.definition: not favored by fortune; marked or accompanied by or resulting in ill fortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest way to mark ill luck, registering that fortune went against someone with none of the ruin *calamitous* insists on.
examples: an unfortunate night for all concerned

entries.definition: (of eggs) no longer edible
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A flat verdict on an egg: not merely aging but past eating, and far blunter about it than *stale*.

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blankest possible condemnation — no mold, no smell, no rot named, just the ruling that the food can no longer be eaten or used.

entries.definition: having lost freshness through passage of time
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Understated to the edge of euphemism: it says only that time has passed and the freshness with it, leaving the eater to reach the conclusion *stale* states outright.
examples: dogs attempting to catch a cold scent

entries.definition: touched by rot or decay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, almost delicate for what it names: rot or decay has only touched the thing, not finished it as in *rotten*.

entries.definition: not fresh today
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a matter of the calendar — it dates the food and leaves the verdict unspoken, where *stale* delivers one.
examples: day-old bread is cheaper than fresh

entries.definition: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disgust made literal: the ruin is not merely named but shown, with the flies' eggs and larvae sitting on it.

entries.definition: dried out
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports a texture rather than a decay — the food has dried out, not gone foul — which makes it the least damning word in the family.
examples: hard dry rolls left over from the day before

entries.definition: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the same infestation as *flyblown*, eggs and larvae alike, but puts the crawling larvae in front of you, which makes it the harder of the two to hear.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A specific and repellent charge — the growth seen on the food or smelled off it — where *bad* offers only a ruling.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of *moldy*, just as exact about mold either seen or smelled.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of the three words for this condition, charging the same mold on the food or smell of mold off it with none of *moldy*'s bluntness.

entries.definition: (used of decomposing oils or fats) having a rank smell or taste usually due to a chemical change or decomposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fixes on fats and oils gone over and on the rank smell or taste that gives them away, a sensory accusation rather than *bad*'s bare ruling.

entries.definition: having decayed or disintegrated; usually implies foulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The word for full collapse — decay carried through to disintegration, and foulness with it.
examples: dead and rotten in his grave

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the same loss — no longer edible or usable — as damage done to the food, a ruin rather than *bad*'s bare verdict.

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of *spoiled*, identical in force and equally final about food past eating or using.
examples: a refrigerator full of spoilt food

entries.definition: lacking freshness, palatability, or showing deterioration from age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word here for the whole slide out of freshness — taste gone, condition gone with age — without yet ruling the food inedible the way *bad* does.

entries.definition: splendid
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise at its plainest - splendid, with none of the awe *sublime* carries or the record standing behind *storied*.
examples: the bright stars of stage and screen

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The illustrious past registered as acclaim - others have noticed, which *historied* does not bother to say.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Excellence pushed past the human scale until it reads as god-given rather than merely achieved.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most rarefied way to say that same god-touched excellence - ornate where *divine* is direct.

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Awe pitched at its loftiest and most ornate, where *sublime* delivers the same awe in a word that can be said plainly.
examples: well-meaning ineptitude that rises to empyreal absurdity

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Matched to *empyreal* in force - awe as sheer altitude, something the eye has to be raised to.

entries.definition: having or deserving or conferring glory
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The family's full measure - glory had, glory deserved and glory handed on, where *illustrious* claims only the having and the conferring.

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same illustrious past stated as plain fact rather than applause, and more formal for it than *celebrated*.

entries.definition: having or conferring glory
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Glory as both possession and gift - it holds glory and lends it out, without *glorious*'s further claim that the glory is deserved.

entries.definition: characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise for a white heat, whether of ardent feeling, of intensity or of sheer brilliance - it burns where *lustrous* only shines.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest of the three - it credits the surpassing excellence to something breathed in from outside without naming the gods as *divine* and *elysian* do.

entries.definition: brilliant
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brilliance as a finish on the surface - it gleams, where *incandescent* burns from inside.
examples: set a lustrous example for others to follow

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The illustrious past turned into something worth recounting - it implies a tale, where *celebrated* implies only admirers.

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Awe that arrests rather than merely pleases - the word here that admits to being overwhelmed.
examples: the sublime beauty of the night

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The shock sits inside the word, so the brutality is reported as something that appals rather than as something merely wrong.

entries.definition: characterized by wickedness or immorality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word in the set made to carry wickedness, and the flatness is its force — *monstrous* shouts where this one only states.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Absolute and unshaded: the wickedness is treated as total rather than as a streak, and no mitigation is offered.
examples: his black heart has concocted yet another black deed

entries.definition: tending to corrupt or pervert
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical in shape: it names an ongoing capacity to spoil rather than passing sentence on a single act.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Suggestive rather than accusing, placing the evil behind what is visible — in what a thing comes out of as much as in the thing itself.
examples: Darth Vader of the dark side

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Attributes the cruelty to a nature rather than a choice, as though it were the whole of what the thing is.
examples: something demonic in him — something that could be cruel

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts design behind the cruelty: intelligence at work, not the blind brutality of *atrocious*.
examples: fires lit up a diabolic scene
diabolical sorcerers under the influence of devils

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The longer form of *diabolic*, and the extra syllable gives it room to sound theatrical rather than clinical.
examples: diabolical sorcerers under the influence of devils

entries.definition: morally bad or wrong
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The bare verdict: it names the wrongness itself and says nothing of the manner, which is what *atrocious* and *fiendish* are for.

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most gleeful of these: the cruelty is relished, ingenuity taking pleasure in itself.

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and bookish where *atrocious* is loud, delivering the same charge of brutality in a cold register.

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weighs the damage rather than the outrage — gravity where *atrocious* offers shock.

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the cruelty outside the human, judging the doer as a kind of creature rather than as someone behaving badly.
examples: no excess was too monstrous for them to commit

entries.definition: tending to corrupt or pervert
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsher than *corruptive*, since what it names does not merely degrade a thing but bends it out of true.

entries.definition: tending to corrupt or pervert
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the influence contagious — something to be kept clear of, not just something to disapprove of.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds menace to the wickedness, so that what it names feels still in motion and threatening rather than simply condemned.
examples: the scheme of some sinister intelligence bent on punishing him

entries.definition: exceedingly sudden and unexpected
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pushes *sudden* past what anyone was braced for, so the speed itself becomes the complaint.
examples: an abrupt change in the weather

entries.definition: marked by abrupt transitions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the transitions as uneven rather than violent — the thing never settles, but nothing in it snaps.

entries.definition: occurring unexpectedly and requiring urgent action
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flat and functional beside *explosive* — the unexpectedness registers only because it compels urgent action, not because it startles.

entries.definition: sudden and loud
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts noise into the suddenness, so where *abrupt* merely catches you unready this one goes off.

entries.definition: sudden and severe
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Grave rather than merely fast: severity is bolted to the speed, so the word reads as a warning.

entries.definition: marked by abrupt transitions
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Harsher than *choppy* on the same broken transitions: the movement snatches, and the word makes it sound ungoverned.

entries.definition: very sudden and in great amount or degree
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures how far the change went as well as how fast it came, which is the dimension *sudden* leaves out.
examples: a sharp drop in the stock market

entries.definition: happening without warning or in a short space of time
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The plain member of the family, covering both arrival without warning and arrival in very little time, and passing no verdict on either.

entries.definition: acting with a specific goal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Purpose read as cold arithmetic - the aim is granted, the warmth withdrawn.
examples: the most calculating and selfish men in the community

entries.definition: acting with a specific goal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flatter, drier twin of *calculating*, closer to bare goal-directedness and lighter on the accusation.

entries.definition: used of persons; emotionally hardened
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most final of the hardened set - the toughness reads as settled all the way through, with nothing soft left to reach.

entries.definition: acting with a specific goal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The darkest reading of the same goal-directedness - purpose taken as plotting rather than planning.

entries.definition: used of persons; emotionally hardened
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal, and the toughness comes with a swagger - the unfeeling is worn rather than lamented.

entries.definition: dispassionate
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Chilly rather than cruel - feeling is simply switched off, and nothing is said about what the coolness is for.

entries.definition: used of persons; emotionally hardened
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain statement of the condition, naming the lost feeling without *hard-boiled*'s relish or *case-hardened*'s finality.

entries.definition: acting with a specific goal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the same purposefulness as *calculating*, but puts the weight on the plan rather than on the coldness of the planner.

entries.definition: acting with a specific goal
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The one word here that credits the goal-directedness, treating aim and judgement as sharpness rather than as a fault.

entries.definition: resembling steel as in hardness
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Not a verdict but a likeness - it measures hardness against metal and leaves the reader to decide whether that is a fault.
examples: steely nerves like those of a steeplejack

entries.definition: scarred by battle
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Here the marks stand as proof of what was come through, so the damage reads as standing earned rather than harm suffered.

entries.definition: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Names the bruise by its two colours, homely and concrete beside the graver *livid*.

entries.definition: separated at the joint
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Structural and bloodless: the joint has come apart, and the word says nothing at all about pain.

entries.definition: separated at the joint
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The exact term for a joint driven out of place, diagnostic where *disjointed* sounds merely come-apart.

entries.definition: having been disembowelled
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most graphic member: the body opened and emptied, damage gone past anything that could still be called a wound.

entries.definition: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The softest word here for real physical injury - it carries the gloss's lean toward battle lightly, and shows nothing of the wound itself.
examples: ambulances … for the hurt men and women

entries.definition: harmed
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The flat report that harm was done, holding back every picture of it that *mangled* insists on showing.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The clipped form for flesh left with jagged edges, cool in shape even though the picture it raises is not.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The ordinary participle for that same ragged tearing, felt rather than measured, where *lacerate* stays curt.

entries.definition: discolored by coagulation of blood beneath the skin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same pooled discoloration in a leaden, grim register that makes the skin sound like something has gone badly wrong beneath it, where *black-and-blue* keeps it almost domestic.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The most violent of these: the jagged edges read as wreckage, the thing ruined rather than merely cut.

entries.definition: having the surface exposed and painful
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports pain rather than shape: the covering is gone and what lies under it is left exposed and stinging, unlike the jagged-edge words beside it.

entries.definition: separated at the joint
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The barest statement of the same parting at the joint — it neither winces nor diagnoses.

entries.definition: having edges that are jagged from injury
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word for a ragged injured edge — it names the tearing and stops, where *mangled* piles on ruin.

entries.definition: suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Graver and more formal than *hurt* for the same injury, dignifying the damage and letting the battlefield sit close without shutting out other harm.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: An everyday word carrying the whole meddling charge, so the disparagement lands quietly where *officious* announces itself.
examples: bustling about self-importantly making an officious nuisance of himself

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Turns the offender into a type, dismissing the whole person rather than the one act *meddling* points to.

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stresses the slowness of it - the ground is taken a little at a time, so no single step looks like the violation that *invasive* makes it sound.
examples: we moved back from the encroaching tide

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flattest of the meddling group - it faults the getting-in-the-way rather than heaping on the contempt that *meddlesome* carries.

entries.definition: tending to intrude (especially upon privacy)
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain term for the fault: it names the pushing-in itself, without the added charge of trespass that *encroaching* carries or the contempt in *meddlesome*.
examples: she felt her presence there was intrusive

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the same unpermitted advance as an incursion, force rather than the patient creep of *encroaching*.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the offensive prying a settled trait of the person, not the single act that *meddling* catches them at.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the deed in progress, where *meddlesome* condemns the character behind it.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cold beside the homely *busybodied*, delivering the same charge of offensive meddling as a verdict rather than a complaint.
examples: bustling about self-importantly making an officious nuisance of himself

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the intrusion in terms of a line crossed without permission, naming the wrong outright where *encroaching* only lets it accumulate.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures the overshoot rather than judging it: a quantity past the mark, not a fault.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The easiest word here to hear without complaint - what lies beyond the requirement can simply be available, where *superfluous* would call the same amount waste.
examples: found some extra change lying on the dresser
extra ribs as well as other supernumerary internal parts

entries.definition: unnecessary and unwarranted
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harshest of these - not merely that the thing was not needed, but that nothing justified it at all.

entries.definition: not absolutely necessary
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The gentlest here - it grants that the thing may well be wanted and withholds only the claim that it is strictly required.

entries.definition: unnecessary and unwarranted
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds the note of waste - unwarranted, and the sting is that it happened anyway; softer in rebuke than *gratuitous*.
examples: a strikers' tent camp … was burned with needless loss of life

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sharper than *excess* - the surplus is treated as serving no purpose, not merely as a quantity over the line.
examples: yet another book on heraldry might be thought redundant
skills made redundant by technological advance

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames what is past the requirement as held in reserve, so it reads as usable rather than as clutter.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, marking the amount as going beyond what was required at all, with a dryness *extra* does not have.
examples: it was supererogatory of her to gloat

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive where *excess* stays quantitative: it says the thing could be stripped away and nothing would be lost.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional and countable - it sets something outside the number required without passing any verdict on it.
examples: extra ribs as well as other supernumerary internal parts

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A ledger word: it registers the amount left over as a balance and carries no complaint about it.
examples: surplus cheese distributed to the needy

entries.definition: unnecessary and unwarranted
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A rebuke rather than an assessment: it says the thing overstepped, where *unnecessary* only says it was not required.

entries.definition: not necessary
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's plain verdict - it states the thing was not needed and leaves any reproach implied rather than spoken, where *gratuitous* speaks it.

entries.definition: not necessary
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatter than *unnecessary* - it reports an absence of need without the faint blame that clings to the other word.

entries.definition: (of a record) having no marks of discredit or offense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise by absence - a record with nothing marked against it, a narrower claim than the completeness *perfect* asserts.

entries.definition: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Reaches past flaw and blemish to impurity as well, so it can clear a substance and not only a performance.
examples: the clear complexion of a healthy young woman

entries.definition: marked by errorless familiarity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Perfection as drilled familiarity - the thing is known so thoroughly that error does not arise, where *errorless* only reports that none did.
examples: had her lines cold before rehearsals started

entries.definition: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Asserts that every necessary quality is present, the opposite test from *flawless*: nothing missing rather than nothing wrong.

entries.definition: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and superlative where *complete* is plain, pitching the same total sufficiency as an accolade.

entries.definition: understood perfectly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the perfection in the grasp rather than in the thing - the understanding is finished, and it says so flatly.

entries.definition: understood perfectly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The idiom tightens *down* into exactness: not merely understood but understood to the letter.

entries.definition: free from error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A flat count of no errors, the coolest word in the family beside *impeccable*'s admiration.

entries.definition: without fault or error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Takes in fault as well as error, so it acquits the conduct and not just the execution.

entries.definition: without a flaw
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Single-minded - one flaw would undo it, where *complete* asks instead whether everything is there.

entries.definition: without fault or error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lifts the same absence of fault into something untouched, admiring where *errorless* is merely accurate.

entries.definition: without fault or error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Reads the absence of fault as a standard held to - admiration rather than measurement.

entries.definition: without fault or error
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Frames faultlessness as something kept intact rather than achieved, and in a stiffer register than *faultless*.

entries.definition: understood perfectly
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dignifies the same perfect understanding as an attainment, where *down* merely reports the state.

entries.definition: being complete of its kind and without defect or blemish
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unqualified standard here, claiming completeness of its kind as well as the absence of blemish, where *flawless* claims only the absence.

entries.definition: without a flaw
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain negation beside *flawless*, denying the flaw without carrying the admiration.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unheated name for the state: impatience or anger without the colouring that *miffed* or *steamed* add to it.

entries.definition: greatly annoyed; out of patience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat, worn British informality, the patience gone by erosion rather than blown out like *steamed*.

entries.definition: greatly annoyed; out of patience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and deflating: a full loss of patience carried in a phrase too offhand to shout, where *exasperated* keeps its composure.

entries.definition: having a strong distaste from surfeit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strong distaste from having had too much of a thing, the surfeited turn of the stomach rather than heat aimed at anyone, and the family's furthest recoil.

entries.definition: not pleased; experiencing or manifesting displeasure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's coolest term: it registers the absence of pleasure and lets it show, without conceding any heat to it.

entries.definition: greatly annoyed; out of patience
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The end of the line, annoyance carried far enough that patience is spent, which is exactly what *annoyed* still holds in reserve.
examples: had an exasperated look on his face

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Friction rather than flare: the same impatience or anger, but felt as something rubbing on and on rather than landing once like *stung*.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Light and slightly diminishing, it sizes the impatience or anger as a small thing and the person holding it as easily put out, where *annoyed* passes no such judgement.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Prickled and smarting: the state as something that caught and stings still, sharper in point than *annoyed* and briefer than *irritated*.
examples: feeling nettled from the constant teasing

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Small and faintly comic, it scales the impatience or anger down to a grievance worth mentioning but not worth raising your voice over.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Vulgar and blunt, it states the same impatience or anger in the coarsest register the family has, which is everything *displeased* withholds.
examples: felt really pissed at her snootiness

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the coarse charge of *pissed* with the particle adding follow-through, anger sent outward rather than merely held.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stirred up rather than simply arrived at: it puts the impatience or anger down to having been worked into someone.
examples: riled no end by his lies

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Churn instead of flare, the impatience or anger turbid and unsettled all through, where *stung* is one sharp point.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pressure made visible, the heat contained but plainly building, hotter than *peeved* and short of the coarseness of *pissed off*.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The state as recoil: something landed, and the impatience or anger is the flinch back from it, where *irritated* only wears on.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Wildness with a threat inside it - the menace is carried by the word itself rather than read in, which is what *untamed* lacks.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The formal counterpart to *feral*, holding the same menace in a stiffer register.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest here - the menace lands as ferocity, where *feral* only marks the wildness as dangerous.

entries.definition: partially wild
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a measure of degree - it places something part-way along the scale and judges it not at all.

entries.definition: not subdued or trained for service or use
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Defined against service - neither subdued nor trained to any use, so the wildness is measured by what the thing has not been made to do.

entries.definition: not domesticated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat negation and nothing more, the plainest term in the family, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

entries.definition: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same natural state as *wild*, but framed as a taming that never happened, so it points at what has not been done to the thing.

entries.definition: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and broad - it covers the animal, the plant and the uncultivated ground alike, naming the natural state without passing any verdict on it.

entries.definition: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the state for what it does to anyone trying to follow it — unordered, unpredictable and confusing at once, where *wild* only says the reins are off.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pitches the uncontrolled feeling high enough to suggest the senses have gone with it, which *excited* never implies.
examples: a crowd of delirious baseball fans

entries.definition: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the same absence of order as *chaotic* but frames it as an order failed rather than an order never present.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unloaded member: it records the uncontrolled excitement and leaves the verdict to whoever is listening.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds hurry and distress to the same uncontrolled feeling, so the energy reads as flailing rather than pleasure.

entries.definition: affected with or marked by frenzy or mania uncontrolled by reason
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reason is overrun rather than loosened, and the word fits both the person seized by the frenzy and the scene that shows it.
examples: the prosecutor's frenzied denunciation of the accused

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and dismissive — it calls the uncontrolled emotion unreason outright instead of merely hinting at it as *delirious* does.

entries.definition: affected with or marked by frenzy or mania uncontrolled by reason
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gives the same reasonless frenzy a clinical ring, where *frenzied* stays pure motion.
examples: outbursts of drunken violence and manic activity and creativity

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coolest word here, naming the control that is missing rather than picturing the emotion that fills the gap.

entries.definition: not brought under control
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat negative that says only that control was never imposed, so it can read as endurance as easily as excess.

entries.definition: marked by extreme lack of restraint or control
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the extremity of the missing restraint without colouring it, and tips negative only because the gloss calls the lack extreme rather than partial.

entries.definition: very difficult to accept or bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one member that concedes the thing can be accepted or borne, at a price the others say is past paying at all.

entries.definition: (used of persons or their behavior) not acceptable or reasonable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Exasperated rather than judicial - it writes a person or their conduct off as beyond dealing with, where *unacceptable* files a ruling.

entries.definition: too extreme to bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the excess itself - the thing has gone past a limit, where *intolerable* simply refuses it without saying by how much.
examples: the insufferable heat of August in a New York apartment with no air conditioning

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat verdict of the three - it rules the thing out rather than measuring what holding it costs, which is what *unbearable* does.

entries.definition: (used of persons or their behavior) not acceptable or reasonable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The cool, formal counterpart of *impossible*: it finds the person or the behaviour unreasonable without any of the heat.

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on whoever is carrying it, so the limit reached is a person's capacity rather than the judgement *intolerable* hands down.

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same limit measured in duration - what cannot be lasted out, where *unbearable* is what cannot be held up under.

entries.definition: too extreme to bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says exactly what *insufferable* says, and the difference is flatness rather than degree.

entries.definition: not able to be supported or defended
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shifts the fault from what cannot be borne to what cannot be defended, so the weakness is in the thing's own standing rather than in anyone's strain.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the unreasonableness first and lets the derision follow as a verdict, where *laughable* starts from the laugh.
examples: the absurd excuse that the dog ate his homework

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and offhand, treating the thing as skewed out of true and waving it away rather than arguing with it.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the scorn in its own body: the thing is not merely open to derision but fit for nothing else.

entries.definition: devoid of good sense or judgment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unadorned charge that good sense or judgement is simply absent, with none of the mockery *ridiculous* invites.

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Almost fond, taking the foolishness as entertainment rather than a fault, a long way from *idiotic*.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hits hardest of these, aiming the derision squarely at whoever produced the thing rather than at the thing itself.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest verdict here, since the derision it invites is a laugh, which can diminish a thing more thoroughly than an attack on it.
examples: a contribution so small as to be laughable

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Theatrical, full-blown absurdity, grander than *laughable* and past the point where argument is possible.
examples: it is ludicrous to call a cottage a mansion

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nothing at all stands behind it, neither intelligence nor thought, a flatter and heavier charge than *foolish*'s bad judgement.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the failure in the sense itself, so nothing coherent is left to answer, where *absurd* still concedes a shape to reject.
examples: ask a nonsensical question and get a nonsensical answer

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and indignant, repudiating the absurdity out loud rather than merely laughing at it as *laughable* does.
examples: a preposterous attempt to turn back the pages of history

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and immediate, the derision arriving without the argument *absurd* implies.
examples: her conceited assumption of universal interest in her rather dull children was ridiculous

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest word here, foolish and ludicrous at a scale too small to be worth condemning.

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the emptiness as blankness rather than stupidity, the intelligence and thought simply not in evidence.

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and colder than *mindless*, treating the absence of intelligence or thought as a settled quality of the thing.

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
